chunks: And by this chain, he said, 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:'
The one who reaches a Penalty (Hadd) regarding (something) in which there is no Penalty (Hadd) (applicable), so he is from the exceeders'.

key_terms.الْمُعْتَدِينَ: The exceeders / those who transgress limits
key_terms.حَدّ: Fixed legal penalty prescribed limit or penalty
key_terms.غَيْرِ حَدٍّ: Something in which there is no fixed penalty applicable

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be among the 'exceeders' when applying a Hadd penalty?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the principle of *al-hadd* (fixed penalty) strictness, warning that arbitrarily applying a specific divine punishment to an act where it is not prescribed constitutes *i'tidad* (transgression/exceeding bounds). In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the precision required in legal rulings to avoid expanding penal categories beyond their textual evidence, ensuring justice remains within defined limits.
